title: 4GE1-style exam questions: urban challenges and sustainable cities (Paper 2, Topics 6.2 and 6.3)
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y11 lesson 28 (Own 4GE1-style exam questions with indicative mark points (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 28: Revision: urban challenges and sustainable cities (Paper 2, Topics 6.2 and 6.3). Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: 'Evaluate strategies to make urban living more sustainable in one named city.' Portal response box.
questions.a: Named city; two or three strategies; benefits and limitations with evidence; roles of different groups; substantiated judgement
questions.model: Teacher plans: intro names the city; P1 transport strategy; P2 housing (brownfield or self-help); P3 waste or energy; conclusion: which works best and why.

questions.q: Compare urban challenges in your two case study cities.
questions.a: Both face housing pressure, but the developed city's issue is cost and the developing city's is informal housing without services; comparison words

questions.q: Explain the role of planners in sustainable urban management.
questions.a: They control land use and approve developments (1), so they can prioritise brownfield sites and transport (1)

questions.q: Explain one challenge of squatter settlements.
questions.a: Lack of clean water and sanitation (1) spreads disease such as cholera (1)
questions.model: Name the challenge: no clean water or sewers. Explain the effect: disease spreads. That is a 2-mark answer: point plus development.

questions.q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of greenfield building.
questions.a: Advantage: cheaper and easier to build (1); disadvantage: loss of countryside and habitats (1)
Work not officially recorded or taxed, such as street selling

questions.q: A squatter settlement is housing built:
questions.a: On land people do not own
options: On land people do not own

questions.q: Big question: what would make your city more sustainable?
questions.a: Reasoned ideas such as brownfield housing, better public transport, green space, recycling and renewable energy
